item.title: Retailers expect 79% of shoppers to use AI tools and shift budgets to cashback apps
item.description:
On Sept. 16, Northwestern University’s Retail Analytics Council and Minty released a survey of 150 senior commerce decision‑makers showing that 79% expect their primary customers to use AI tools by 2027. Eighty‑one percent of participants said cashback and savings tools were the most helpful marketing channel for shoppers, outranking traditional ads, loyalty programs, retail media and creator marketing.
Ninety‑eight percent of the surveyed executives came from firms with annual revenue over $100 million. Two‑thirds of marketers said they believe AI will be the primary way to reach shoppers in 2027, while half are already marketing directly to AI agents. Among those targeting early‑stage AI shoppers, 61% have increased or reallocated budgets toward cashback and savings apps.
“This isn’t marketers tweaking a line item,” Frank Dudley, associate director of the Retail Analytics Council at Northwestern University said.
Digital Commerce 360 and Bizrate Insights’ 2026 survey found that finding better deals was the top reason shoppers used AI tools. The current study shows AI platforms are increasingly shaping where and how customers shop online.
Source: Digital Commerce 360 (https://digitalcommerce360.com/2026/09/17/ecommerce-trends-how-marketing-budgets-are-adapting-to-ai-driven-purchases)

item.title: Raspberry AI upgrades its platform with generative agents to cut sampling time by up to 60%
item.description:
Raspberry AI today announced an upgrade to its platform that adds generative AI agents and can reduce sampling time by up to 60 percent. The company said 70 percent of its active customers now use the AI across more than three departments, up from 30 percent in April.
The upgrade enables the AI agents to assist with tasks ranging from initial design sketches to merchandising, wholesale, marketing and e‑commerce execution. Kate Spade’s Loop Small Flap Bag was created using the earlier version of the tool, which Lissette Siesholtz said saved her team about two weeks of sampling. Other brands listed as Raspberry AI clients include Skims, Alo and Walmart. The generative AI agents can now generate product descriptions, pricing suggestions and promotional copy alongside visual designs. Lissette Siesholtz noted that the earlier AI tool cut the need for physical samples, allowing the team to finalize the bag design faster. The upgrade means the AI agents can now work across design, merchandising, wholesale, marketing and e‑commerce, moving from concept to actual commerce.
“We used Raspberry AI to create our loop small flap shoulder bag—inputting sketch ideas, prompting, iterating, until we landed on exactly the right design. It saved our team about two weeks of sampling,” Lissette Siesholtz, senior director of technical design at Tapestry said.
“70 percent of the startup’s active customers now use its AI across more than three departments. In April, this number was just 30 percent,” Cheryl Liu, founder and CEO of Raspberry AI said.
Before the upgrade, Raspberry AI’s primary offering turned designer sketches into photorealistic renderings to show how fabrics would fit and drape in real life. The company said that feature could reduce a brand’s sampling time and costs by as much as 60 percent. This capability had already been adopted by labels such as Kate Spade, Skims, Alo and Walmart.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/talk-to-my-agent-amazon-ecomid-kate-spade-raspberry-1239239965)

item.title: Polybion expands Celium biomaterial into everyday products beyond runway
item.description:
Polybion’s Celium sheet material appeared in three looks from designer Patricio Campillo’s spring 2027 collection shown at New York Fashion Week. The material is now being tested in custom menu covers for Siari Ritz‑Carlton Reserve restaurants, made‑to‑order lamps from Natural Urbano, and cardholders for energy firm Sujío.
Celium is offered in two versions: the translucent, lightweight Manto and the denser, more tactile Espumante. Both versions can be cut, shaped and integrated into products such as leather‑like accessories, lighting fixtures and packaging. Polybion says the biomaterial is positioned as a substitute for leather, synthetic leather and coated textiles in consumer goods.
Before these trials, Polybion’s Celium had mainly been featured on fashion runways, most recently in a New York Fashion Week presentation. The material’s earlier use focused on apparel rather than objects subject to repeated handling.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/sustainability/material-world-polybion-celium-arda-spent-grain-1239240299)

item.title: Panama Canal Projects 29.5 Daily Transits for FY2027 Amid El Niño Drought
item.description:
The Panama Canal Authority projects an average of 29.5 vessel transits per day for fiscal year 2027, which begins October 1, as El Niño‑driven drought curtails water supply. That forecast marks an 18% drop from the typical 36 transits the waterway normally handles.
The authority also expects 10,750 high‑draft transits for the fiscal year, a 6.5% decline from the prior budgeted level. Despite fewer ships, total revenue is forecast to rise 6.7% to $5.56 billion, with transit revenue climbing 5.7% to about $5.41 billion thanks to a shift toward higher‑value LNG and LPG cargo. Under a drought scenario for February‑May 2027, Neopanamax vessels could face a 44‑foot draft limit, reducing cargo capacity, while the canal maintains its current 48‑foot maximum draft pending reassessment of Gatún Lake levels.
“Even when there are 38 ships going through in a day, the administrator says only three spots are usually auctioned off,” Ilya Espino de Marotta, Administrator of the Panama Canal Authority said.
“the daily transit average could be reduced to 29. She said the limit would “probably not” be lowered to 24 slots,” Ilya Espino de Marotta, Administrator of the Panama Canal Authority said.
Officials had previously reduced the daily transit estimate to 32 as drought conditions worsened, and the canal saw transits fall to as low as 22 ships per day during the mid‑2023 to early 2024 drought. Panama declared a national emergency over El Niño in August, and the ACP warned that continued low rainfall could force further operational cuts. The current outlook reflects concerns of a repeat of that earlier dry spell.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/logistics/panama-canal-el-nino-drought-daily-transit-cuts-2027-budget-tarade-1239242556)

item.title: Jordan Brand launches strength‑training gear line with Oct. 13 release at NikeStrength.com and Dick’s Sporting Goods
item.description:
Jordan Brand introduces Jordan Strength, a six‑piece strength‑training equipment set, slated for release on Oct. 13 via NikeStrength.com and selected Dick’s Sporting Goods stores. The line comprises dumbbells, kettlebells, barbells, an adjustable bench, a soft plyo box and a half‑rack with storage.
The equipment is marketed as inspired by basketball legend Michael Jordan and is intended for both home gyms and professional facilities. Nike says the launch is part of its effort to broaden the Jordan brand beyond footwear amid broader challenges in its apparel segments. In its latest financial update, Nike reported a 1% year‑over‑year revenue decline in Q4 to $11 billion, with full‑year sales holding steady at $46 billion. The company also lowered its outlook for the first half of the next fiscal year, forecasting a low‑ to mid‑single‑digit sales drop.
“The demotion “underlines the company’s broader problems and its loss of value as it tries to get the business back on track,” Neil Saunders, GlobalData managing director, told Retail Dive earlier this month,” Neil Saunders, GlobalData managing director said.
“Nike has been quietly closing its neighborhood local stores across the country, as part of a larger strategy to “create Nike’s future marketplace,” a company spokesperson told Retail Dive,” Company spokesperson said.
Nike’s CEO Elliott Hill noted last year that the firm was working to rebalance its footwear mix and reduce reliance on legacy lines such as Air Force 1, Air Jordan and Dunk. He later warned on an earnings call that Nike Sportswear and Jordan Streetwear were not meeting potential, with weak sell‑through affecting discounts and future orders.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/jordan-brand-debuts-strength-training-equipment-line/830659)

item.title: Nike adds LVMH executive Alexandre Arnault to board as turnaround continues
item.description:
Nike announced on Wednesday that Alexandre Arnault, deputy CEO of LVMH’s Moët Hennessy division, will join its board of directors. Arnault has led the wine and spirits unit since February 2025 and previously oversaw the acquisition of Rimowa, which he ran for four years.
He also worked at Tiffany & Co. and McKinsey & Company before his current role. Nike said the appointment aims to bring innovation and brand‑building expertise to its turnaround effort. The move follows a week after news that Nike would be dropped from the S&P 100 index. Recently Nike has reset its online distribution in China, launched a Studio Fleece line, named a new CFO and a commercial chief, and cut its store count by 4% as it closes small‑format Nike Live stores.
“Alexandre has earned a reputation for helping iconic global brands evolve, innovate and grow in a changing, complex marketplace,” Nike Executive Chairman Mark Parker said.
“Alexandre understands how some of the world's most influential brands stay relevant, deepen consumer connections and drive long-term growth, His experience across innovation, digital transformation and brand building will be an asset as we continue to strengthen our connection with consumers, sharpen our competitive edge and accelerate Nike's next chapter of growth around the world,” Nike CEO Elliott Hill said.
Nike’s turnaround has been dragging as lifestyle demand slows and competition heats up. The company recently reset its online distribution in China, launched a Studio Fleece line, named a new CFO and a commercial chief, and reduced its store count by 4% while closing small‑format Nike Live stores. Analysts note a worsening top line, a four‑year decline in product purchase obligations, and double‑digit drops in Converse and China.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/nike-adds-lvmh-exec-alexandre-arnault-board-innovation-turnaround/830662)

item.title: Amazon raises U.S. hourly starting wage to $20 and adds new grocery and banking benefits.
item.description:
Amazon announced Wednesday that it is increasing the minimum hourly starting wage for full-time core operations employees in the United States by $1 to $20 per hour. Starting in October, all U.S. Amazon employees will receive an uncapped 10% discount on groceries and essentials bought online through Amazon.com or Whole Foods Market, and a 20% discount when shopping in Whole Foods stores. The company said the higher base pay lifts the average starting wage to about $24 per hour, and its new Day 1 Financial banking benefit will be introduced later this year and become widely available by 2027.
The Day 1 Financial benefit gives employees a membership in First Tech Federal Credit Union that carries no overdraft fees, no monthly maintenance fees, and no minimum balance requirements for standard checking and savings accounts. Through the same program, workers can apply for auto and home loans, and the service does not require a credit history to open an account. The grocery discount is uncapped and can be combined with any existing Prime member discounts, and all Amazon employees already receive a complimentary Prime membership. This new banking layer supplements Amazon’s current Brightside Financial Care service, which provides employees with free access to a financial assistant for budgeting, debt planning, and other money‑management tasks.

item.title: AlixPartners forecasts 4‑7% U.S. holiday sales growth as shoppers shift tactics
item.description:
AlixPartners released its U.S. Retail Holiday Outlook on Wednesday, forecasting 4 to 7 percent sales growth for the holiday season. Despite inflationary pressures, the report notes that actual spending has averaged roughly 5 percent above prior‑year levels each month throughout 2026. The outlook is based on a poll of more than 15,000 U.S. consumers surveyed over the year, which found 57 percent saying the economy is worse than a year ago and 37 percent planning to spend less this holiday.
Shoppers are responding by trading down to private‑label or mid‑tier brands only where they believe quality holds up, with high‑income households now spending over 50 percent more on private label than in 2019. Traffic at value retailers and off‑price stores rose 5 percent year‑over‑year, while trips to full‑price apparel stores fell 9 percent, and 47 percent of consumers plan to start holiday shopping before Halloween, up from 43 percent last year.
“Across the industry, retailers are wondering when consumers will stop showing up given the declining sentiment trajectory we’ve been seeing for the last few years,” Bryan Eshelman, Americas lead of retail at AlixPartners said.
“Even high-income households are moving in this direction, spending over 50 percent more on private label than in 2019,” the report’s authors said.
Industry analysts have said that up to half of the sales gain is due to inflation. In this year’s study, 57 percent of consumers say the economy is worse than it was 12 months ago, up six percentage points from last year, and 37 percent intend to spend less this holiday season (plus-2 points from last year), the report noted. The data showed that 47 percent of consumers polled said they plan to start shopping before Halloween, which compares to 43 percent last year.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/shoppers-keep-spending-but-shift-strategies-alix-partners-1239239745)

item.title: Toys R Us adds 120 stand‑alone stores for holiday season
item.description:
Toys R Us announced it will open 120 new stand-alone stores across the United States this holiday season. The expansion, done with Go Retail Group, will increase the retailer’s stand‑alone footprint to 160 locations.
Selected stores will include Creator Studios for influencer and brand content, as well as candy shops and cafes. Outside stand‑alone locations, Toys R Us operates shop‑in‑shop concepts in Macy’s stores nationwide, at airports and with the Navy Exchange Service Command. The company opened a shop‑in‑shop at Orlando International Airport in August and plans a second for next summer, while FAO Schwarz launched a new Amazon storefront this week.
“This is a major moment for Toys R Us as we significantly expand our presence across the United States,” Jamie Uitdenhowen, executive vice president of Toys R Us at WHP Global said.
Last year Toys R Us opened over 30 stores, including flagships and seasonal holiday shops. The brand emerged from a 2017 Chapter 11 bankruptcy and 2018 liquidation as Tru Kids, before WHP Global acquired a controlling stake in 2021.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/toys-r-us-accelerates-store-openings-holidays/830637)

item.title: Mexico lifts empty-truck ban at Eagle Pass after 700 tractors stranded
item.description:
Mexican customs authorities lifted the empty-truck restriction at the Eagle Pass–Piedras Negras crossing on Monday, ending a five‑day halt that left nearly 700 tractors stranded on the U.S. side. The move restores normal flow at a crossing that typically handles about 1,000 commercial vehicles daily and processes roughly $3.8 billion in annual trade.
The restriction, in place since September 9, had permitted loaded trucks to enter Mexico but barred empty trailers and tractors operating without trailers from crossing southbound. As a result, commercial traffic at the Eagle Pass international bridges fell from roughly 1,000 trucks per day to between 300 and 400, according to the city’s bridge director. The regional export manufacturing association estimated that the halt could have imposed logistics losses of up to $1 million per day on dependent manufacturers and carriers. The reversal followed talks on Monday between industry representatives, ANAM, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and the Mexican Consulate, and it also averted a planned trucker protest at the crossing.
Mexico’s National Customs Agency (ANAM) imposed the empty‑truck restriction on southbound crossings at Piedras Negras on September 9, allowing only freight‑laden trucks to pass. The measure was initially said to remain in effect until further notice, and by Monday nearly 700 tractors were stranded in Eagle Pass without a way to return to Mexico.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/mexico-lifts-empty-truck-restriction-after-700-tractors-stranded-at-border)

item.title: Ravel secures $8.2 million to scale elastane-free polyester recycling
item.description:
Ravel raised $8.2 million in an oversubscribed seed round to advance its blended-textile recycling technology from a Seattle pilot toward commercial scale. The pilot handles 20-24 metric tons of material each year, while the company aims for its first commercial lines to process about 10,000 metric tons annually.
Ravel’s Purification Recycling washes away elastane, dyes and other contaminants while keeping the underlying PET polymer intact, avoiding shredding or depolymerization. The resulting recycled polyester can enter existing fiber, yarn and fabric production lines without a green premium or subsidy. Initial feedstock will come from post-industrial waste such as cutting scraps from apparel factories, which the company says offers consistent quality near production hubs.
“The technology works. We know how to scale it. We’re proving that out,” Zahlen Titcomb, co‑founder and CEO said.
Elastane gives performance apparel its stretch but can make the surrounding polyester difficult to recycle. Conventional mechanical recycling shreds textiles into lower‑grade fibers, while chemical recycling breaks PET into monomers, both of which are hindered by the presence of elastane. Ravel says its process avoids those steps, preserving the PET polymer for reuse in existing supply chains.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/ravel-funding-polyester-elastane-textile-recycling-1239239050)

item.title: Whatnot cuts commissions for high-volume sellers, takes aim at eBay Live
item.description:
Whatnot announced that, starting September 21 for existing sellers and the week of September 28 for new ones, it will shift to volume‑based commissions that can drop to 6.5% for sellers with over $500,000 in four‑week sales. The new tiers also list publicly available rates as low as 4.5% for fashion and 4% for other collectibles, with coins able to fall to 3.5%.
For sellers with less than $15,000 in sales over a four‑week period, the standard US commission stays at 8% across most categories. Total sales from Live shows, Marketplace and Shop are combined to determine the four‑week volume, and the commission applied to each sale depends on its category. Payment processing remains separate at 2.9% plus $0.30 per transaction in the US, calculated on the full amount paid by the buyer including shipping and taxes. Premier Shop sellers receive an extra 10% discount on their commission rate through October 31, but that benefit ends on November 1, after which rates will be based solely on sales volume.
While Whatnot does not name eBay directly, it frames the change as a reaction to the three‑decade‑old ecommerce giant’s effort to gain ground in livestream shopping after years of inactivity. In July, eBay introduced uniform Live fees, setting a 4% commission plus 2.9% processing for coins and eligible sneakers and a 6% commission plus 2.9% processing for most other categories.
Source: Value Added Resource (https://valueaddedresource.net/whatnot-cuts-fees-high-volume-sellers)

item.title: MoneyGram partners with Rain to launch stablecoin-backed card in Colombia
item.description:
MoneyGram announced on September 10 that it will work with stablecoin payments firm Signify Holdings, doing business as Rain, to create a digital payments card that lets users hold stablecoins, access cash and pay via Visa’s network. The company plans to issue a physical card option before the end of the year and will first roll out the card in Colombia.
Customers will be able to add the card to Apple or Google wallets for digital use. The physical card will allow ATM cash withdrawals and in‑person purchases where digital cards are less accepted. MoneyGram says its services reach 200 countries and territories worldwide. The new card is stablecoin‑backed and is not tied to a traditional bank account or fiat currency balance.
“The new card takes a “fundamentally different approach that combines the benefits of stablecoins with a seamless customer experience for everyday utility” and is “built directly into the MoneyGram app,” a spokesperson for the company said by email said.
“The card is stablecoin-backed and is not a traditional bank account or fiat-currency balance,” a spokesperson for the company said said.
MoneyGram had previously offered a physical fiat‑based debit card that was discontinued in December 2025. Signify Holdings also provides a similar stablecoin‑backed card to Western Union, which launched its version in August. The move follows the passage of the Genius Act last year, which created a regulatory framework for stablecoin use in the United States.
Source: Payments Dive (https://paymentsdive.com/news/moneygram-taps-stablecoin-ally/830673)

item.title: Greggs Overtakes Costa to Lead UK Branded Coffee Shops with 2,737 Outlets
item.description:
Greggs overtook Costa Coffee to become the UK’s largest branded coffee shop operator, with 2,737 outlets versus Costa’s 2,707, according to Allegra World Coffee Portal’s 2026 report. The UK branded coffee shop market grew 3.5% in 2025 to 12,313 outlets, while sales increased 5.5% to £6.8bn.
Greggs opened 34 new shops during the first half of 2026, bringing its estate to 2,773 locations by the end of June. The retailer reported total sales of £1.1bn for the first half of 2026, up 7.2% year on year, with like-for-like sales in company-managed shops rising 2.1%. Greggs is targeting around 100 to 110 net new openings in 2026 and has identified potential for at least 3,500 UK shops over the longer term. Costa responded by relaunching scones after a five‑year gap and launching an Afternoon Bundle that pairs a hot or iced drink with a scone served with jam and cream.
Before this shift, Costa Coffee had held the lead as the UK’s largest branded coffee chain.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/09/greggs-overtakes-costa)

item.title: Food Lion plans to open six more stores in Carolinas and Georgia by year-end
item.description:
Food Lion announced on Tuesday that it will add six new stores across North Carolina, South Carolina and Georgia before the end of 2026. These openings, together with four stores launched earlier in 2026, will bring the chain’s total new-store count for the year to ten, a sharp increase from the single net additions in fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2025.
The four stores opened so far this year are two each in North Carolina and South Carolina. The six additional stores planned for later 2026 include two in North Carolina, three in South Carolina, and one in Georgia, with a Summerfield, NC store opening next Wednesday; Charlotte, NC; Lavonia, GA; and Greenville, SC stores opening in October; a Hilton Head, SC store debuting in November; and a Wren, SC store opening in December. All new locations will feature ready-to-eat, ready-to-cook, and ready-to-heat meals, the Local Goodness program of regionally sourced items, and pickup or home delivery via the Food Lion website, app, and third-party platforms such as Instacart, DoorDash, and Uber Eats. Meanwhile, Food Lion is remodeling 93 stores in the Greensboro, NC market, aiming to finish the work later this year, and is preparing similar updates in the Richmond and Roanoke, VA markets per CFO Jolanda Poots-Bijl’s August remarks to investors.
The expansion follows Ahold Delhaize’s 2025 announcement of an automated grocery distribution center in Burlington, North Carolina, and the subsequent ground-breaking on that facility in February 2026 to boost fresh and frozen food supply to Food Lion stores in the state. Prior to this year’s acceleration, the chain had added just one net new store in each of fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2025.
Source: Grocery Dive (https://grocerydive.com/news/food-lion-grows-store-footprint-carolinas-georgia-grocery/830604)

item.title: Truckload carriers cut approved carrier list to 14,000 as capacity exodus continues
item.description:
Truckload carriers reduced their approved carrier lists to 14,000 from a peak of 60,000, executives said at an investor conference this week. Filter said there aren’t 100,000 carriers he considers safe enough to operate on the road.
The broker liability ruling handed down by the Supreme Court a year ago has forced brokers and shippers to vet carriers more strictly, contributing to the shrinkage of approved lists. A Texas Supreme Court case involving Home Depot determined that retailers meet liability obligations by hiring reputable carriers, reinforcing the trend toward stricter partner selection. Regulatory pressure on sham driver schools and ELD oversight has further limited the influx of new operators, while diesel price spikes have strained small fleets. Filter noted that the forced closure of sham driver schools has narrowed the entry point for new carriers, ensuring only those with proper training can obtain authority.
“I can tell you that there aren’t 100,000 carriers out there that I think any of us would be able to look at and say, 100,000 carriers are safe and should be out there on the road,” Jim Filter, President and CEO, Schneider National said.
“Well, with the amount of supply that has exited, it has created enough demand for our services,” Jim Filter, President and CEO, Schneider National said.
The truckload capacity correction is still in the “early innings,” carrier executives said at an investor conference this week. A regulatory crackdown launched a year ago compounded the impact of prolonged economic weakness, which had already forced numerous small and midsize fleets out of the industry. The recent surge in diesel fuel prices has further plagued small operators, many of whom don’t have recovery mechanisms in place.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/carriers-tl-capacity-exodus-growing-not-slowing)

item.title: Norfolk Southern launches daily rail link from Charleston port to Huntsville
item.description:
Norfolk Southern launched a daily rail service from the Port of Charleston to Huntsville, Alabama, on September 11 to expand rail access to Southeast markets. The service aims to extend the port’s reach to markets in North Alabama and Middle Tennessee, where about 25% of SC Ports’ cargo currently moves by rail.
Customers can transfer containers at intermodal hubs in Atlanta, Birmingham, Memphis, Nashville, Charlotte, and Louisville for faster connectivity to inland destinations. Last year SC Ports finished a $55 million expansion of its Inland Port Greer facility, which raised cargo capacity by 50% and added 9,000 feet of rail track to accommodate longer trains. In August the port agreed with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to study deepening the channel at its North Charleston terminal, a move that could support larger vessels and speed up logistics. Norfolk Southern already runs a daily and overnight train to Inland Port Greer, located along the I-85 corridor between Atlanta and Charlotte.
“Deepening the channel could help drive cargo growth and ensure expedited logistics for shippers,” Micah Mallace, President and CEO of SC Ports said.
SC Ports has been investing in infrastructure to boost competitiveness, including the recent $55 million Inland Port Greer expansion. Norfolk Southern already provides a daily and overnight rail service to Inland Port Greer, linking the port to the Atlanta‑Charlotte corridor. The new Huntsville service builds on those links to reach deeper into the Southeast interior.
Source: Supply Chain Dive (https://supplychaindive.com/news/sc-ports-norfolk-southerns-intermodal-service-grows-southeast-reach/830582)

item.title: Los Angeles and Long Beach ports propose $60 per visit incentive for zero-emission trucks
item.description:
The Port of Los Angeles and the Port of Long Beach proposed a three-year incentive program offering $60 per terminal visit and up to $36,000 annually for zero-emission trucks, according to a Sept. 15 press release. Comments on the draft proposal are accepted through Nov. 2, with a virtual public hearing scheduled for Sept. 29 from 10 a.m. to noon. The program builds on a 2023 commitment to provide $60 million in vouchers for zero-emission Class 8 drayage trucks at the San Pedro Bay complex.
The incentive pays $60 for each terminal visit made by a qualifying zero-emission truck, capped at $36,000 per vehicle each year. It runs for three years and is intended to offset the higher ownership and operating costs of zero‑emission drayage trucks. Participating trucks must operate at either the Port of Los Angeles or the Port of Long Beach to earn the reward. The measure is part of the ports' Clean Air Action Plan, which targets zero emissions for on‑road drayage trucks by 2035.
“This incentive program is another tool in our decarbonization playbook, helping offset the higher costs of owning and operating zero-emission trucks based on direct feedback from truckers about what they need,” Dr. Noel Hacegaba, CEO of the Port of Long Beach said.
The proposal is part of the ports' shared Clean Air Action Plan, which first launched in 2006 and has been updated twice, aiming for zero emissions from on-road drayage trucks by 2035. It follows a 2023 initiative in which the ports pledged $60 million in vouchers to help acquire zero-emission Class 8 drayage trucks for the San Pedro Bay complex.
Source: Supply Chain Dive (https://supplychaindive.com/news/san-pedro-ports-seek-zero-emission-truck-usage-boost-via-new-incentive-prog/830536)

item.title: Senate blocks Clarity Act as vote fails 50-49
item.description:
The Senate rejected the Clarity Act on Tuesday, with a 50-49 vote against advancing the cryptocurrency regulation bill. The bill would have required 60 votes to pass, leaving regulators to shape crypto policy without new legislation.
The legislation would have barred crypto firms from offering stablecoin rewards deemed economically equivalent to interest-bearing bank deposits, a provision negotiated by Senators Tillis and Angela Alsobrooks. It also included a temporary measure allowing the Treasury secretary to limit those rewards if community banks experienced deposit flight, expiring after 18 months. Opposition cited concerns over former President Trump’s $1.4 billion crypto income and fears that the bill’s ethics loopholes could let officials profit from digital‑asset rules. The legislation would have let state attorneys general prohibit public officials from issuing, sponsoring or holding significant interests in digital assets, with an exemption for Trump’s sons who run his family’s crypto venture.
“While [regulators] can make rules, those are less stable and permanent than legislation,” Austin Campbell, adjunct professor at New York University said.
The House passed a version of the Clarity Act last year, but the bill stalled in the Senate after months of negotiation over stablecoin yield and ethics provisions. Democratic lawmakers and state attorneys general warned the legislation would weaken their ability to combat crypto fraud, while Republicans introduced updated ethics rules aimed at restricting public officials’ crypto holdings. With Congress set to adjourn in early October and not return until after the November midterms, the bill’s prospects for revival appear slim.
Source: Payments Dive (https://paymentsdive.com/news/clarity-act-fails-senate-trump-crypto-conflict-of-interest-sec-cftc/830651)

item.title: Norfolk Southern sees intermodal volume jump 13.7% as it shifts focus to ease of use
item.description:
Norfolk Southern reported a 13.7% year-over-year increase in intermodal volume for the past week, indicating the railroad is shifting focus from price competition to making rail freight easier to buy, plan, monitor, and use. Speaking at the Intermodal Association of North America’s annual conference in Long Beach, vice president Shawn Tureman, who has 23 years at the railroad, said the industry’s central challenge has moved from competing on cost to removing friction in the customer experience.
Norfolk Southern divides its intermodal history into three eras: building the network, competing for the customer, and now removing friction that constrains rail’s ability to win freight from trucks. The first era involved constructing terminals, double‑stack routes, port connections, and corridors that gave the railroad the most extensive East Coast intermodal network. The second era focused on competing for customers but left shippers to adapt operations to the railroad rather than receiving a service designed around their needs. The current phase aims to make rail freight simple, reliable, and visible so shippers choose it consistently over truck moves.
“Cost alone does not shift a supply chain,” said Tureman.“Customers need confidence,” Shawn Tureman, vice president of Automotive & Intermodal Marketing said.
Following railroad consolidation in the late 1990s, Class I railroads invested extensively in intermodal terminals, double-stack routes, port connections, and long-haul freight corridors. Those investments created the backbone of the U.S. intermodal system and established rail as a viable long-distance alternative to highway transportation.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/norfolk-southern-new-intermodal-era-about-removing-rail-friction)

item.title: WiseTech warns ocean freight booking risk stays elevated on Asia‑North America and Asia‑Europe lanes
item.description:
WiseTech Global’s new Ocean Freight Risk Outlook says freight risk will remain elevated over the next four weeks on the key Asia‑North America and Asia‑Europe trades, driven by booking acceptance risk and weak service reliability. On the Asia‑North America lane, the demand‑to‑supply ratio is forecast to rise from 76% in week 37 to 100% in week 38 before easing to 79% and then 91%, while booking security risk is expected to stay at or above its historical average, climbing just above 40% later in the period.
Monthly on‑time performance for Asia‑North America fell from 43% in May to 33.9% in August, with weekly performance dropping to 29.4% in week 35, making one‑to‑three‑day delays the most common outcome.
“Multiple factors are at play, and the type of resulting risk varies significantly by trade lane,” Jon Charles, product manager at WiseTech said.
“For freight forwarders and cargo owners, Mr Charles said the consequences could include difficulty securing space, longer or less predictable lead times, and higher inventory and supply chain costs,” Jon Charles, product manager at WiseTech said.
Source: The Loadstar (https://theloadstar.com/ocean-freight-booking-risk-remains-elevated-wisetech-warns)

item.title: Heal’s appoints former Liberty managing director Sarah Coonan as CEO effective 1 October 2026
item.description:
Heal’s has named Sarah Coonan, formerly managing director at Liberty, as its new chief executive, with her start date set for 1 October 2026. Coonan spent over 15 years at Liberty after a four‑year stint at Harrods, and she succeeds Hamish Mansbridge, who is stepping down after 11 years as CEO.
Mansbridge joined Heal’s in 2015 and during his tenure led the refurbishment of the Tottenham Court Road flagship, expanded the retailer’s regional store base and grew its digital channel. He also oversaw the Heal’s Discovers programme, which supports established and emerging design talent. Heal’s, which has been designing, making and selling furniture for more than two centuries, recently launched its AW26 ‘Modern Heirlooms’ collection across stores and online. Coonan said she feels privileged to join a brand with a rich history and looks forward to building on its foundations while evolving it for the next generation of customers.
“Heal’s is far more than a retail business; for more than two centuries it has sat at the intersection of culture, heritage and design, shaping the way we think about our homes and the spaces around us,” said Mansbridge, “I am incredibly proud of what we have achieved and look forward to watching the next phase of growth under Sarah’s leadership,” Hamish Mansbridge, outgoing CEO of Heal’s said.
Mansbridge joined Heal’s in 2015 and during his tenure the retailer revamped its Tottenham Court Road flagship, developed its regional retail presence and expanded its digital offering. He also oversaw initiatives including Heal’s Discovers, which supports established and emerging design talent.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/09/heals-liberty-sarah-coonan)

item.title: Amazon delivers over 2 million summer meals to rural students
item.description:
Amazon delivered more than 2 million free summer meals to students in rural areas across 13 states this summer. That represents a nearly thirty‑fold increase from the pilot in 2025, which provided just over 71,000 meals.
The Summer Meals for Kids program, run with No Kid Hungry and 18 local food‑bank and school‑district partners, uses Amazon’s rural delivery network to pick up shelf‑stable meal boxes and deliver them to families’ doorsteps within 24 to 72 hours at no cost. Partners receive Amazon’s logistics tools, including an order‑creation portal, package tracking and eight weeks of onboarding support before the summer season begins. The initiative operates under the USDA’s Summer Food Service Program, which funds free meals for children when school is out. Since 2020, Amazon’s broader food‑security effort has moved more than 60 million meals from food banks to families nationwide.
“Amazon's delivery network already reaches some of the most remote communities in America every single day,” said Kadie Newman, vice president of transportation services at Amazon,” Kadie Newman, vice president of transportation services at Amazon said.
“We've heard from rural families across the country that they value the convenience and nutrition that home delivery could offer in the summer,” said Courtney Smith, senior vice president of program research, innovation, and impact at No Kid Hungry,” Courtney Smith, senior vice president of program research, innovation, and impact at No Kid Hungry said.
The program began as a pilot in 2025 with three partners, delivering over 71,000 meals. One year later it expanded to 18 partners across 13 states.
Source: About Amazon (https://aboutamazon.com/news/community/amazon-summer-meals-kids-rural-delivery)

item.title: Tesco adds 400 new styles to F&F Online and launches London Fashion Week pop-up
item.description:
Tesco has expanded its F&F Online fashion offer with 400 new styles and enhanced search tools, while opening a pop-up shop at Frameless Gallery on 18 September. The pop-up will be open to the public from 12.30 pm to 4 pm, coinciding with the start of London Fashion Week.
The refreshed online experience across Tesco’s web and app now includes hundreds of additional styles, more size options and exclusive online ranges. Enhanced search functionalities and curated styling inspiration aim to help shoppers discover and assemble complete outfits with greater confidence. The pop‑up at Frameless Gallery, Marble Arch offers an interactive space where customers can shop the new F&F A/W collection and experience the brand’s updated look and feel. Tesco noted that F&F’s annual clothing sales have surpassed £1 billion and the brand grew 5.1 % in the 2025/26 fiscal year.
“Our refreshed online offer across web and app brings customers more fashion choice than ever before, including hundreds of additional styles, more sizes and exclusive online ranges, as well as enhanced search tools and curated styling inspiration, making it easier to discover and shop complete outfits with confidence,” Katja Ahola Klamkin, managing director of Home & Clothing at Tesco said.
The update builds on Tesco’s earlier relaunch of F&F Online, which had already refreshed the brand’s digital presence.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/09/tesco-builds-on-successful-ff-online-launch-with-revamped-shopping-experience)

item.title: FTC orders Amway to pay $225 million for deceptive MLM practices
item.description:
The Federal Trade Commission and the state of Washington announced that Amway and two of its affiliates will pay $225 million to settle allegations that they used unfair and deceptive tactics to recruit members into their multilevel marketing opportunity. The payment represents the largest monetary recovery ever obtained in an FTC action against a multilevel marketing company. The complaint alleges that Amway misled prospective business owners with promises of earnings exceeding $40,000 a year and then pressured them to buy products they could not resell.
The order requires Amway, World Wide Group, and Leadership Team Development to provide redress to consumers harmed by the alleged deceptive practices, with nearly all of the $225 million going to affected individuals. The FTC and Washington state said the companies falsely told independent business owners they could earn substantial income, replace a full-time job, or retire early, while most participants who joined after 2020 spent more on products and training than they received. Additionally, the agencies alleged that Amway and its affiliates misrepresented the likelihood of recruiting multiple new members and the exclusivity of mentorship from top leaders, when in fact most recruits did not bring in others and the mentors were not highly successful. The affiliates’ training programs reportedly instructed owners to purchase a set volume of products each month regardless of resale potential and to focus efforts on recruiting others to duplicate that behavior.
“Amway and its affiliates misled prospective workers with false earnings claims and then pressured them to buy Amway products they were unlikely to be able to sell,” Christopher Mufarrige, Director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection said.
Amway describes itself as one of the largest multilevel marketing companies in the United States. World Wide Group and Leadership Team Development are two of its biggest approved provider groups, selling training
Source: FTC Press Releases (https://ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2026/09/ftc-takes-historic-action-against-multilevel-marketing-operator-amway-unfair-deceptive-business)

item.title: FTC approves expanded automatic Amazon Prime refunds, raising cap to $200
item.description:
The Federal Trade Commission said in September 2026 that Amazon will accelerate and broaden refunds to consumers under its $2.5 billion Prime‑enrollment settlement. Under a court‑approved revision, the maximum refund per consumer rises from $51 to $200 and payments will be made automatically, with the first round for users of 11‑20 Prime benefits beginning October 1, 2026.
As of September 2026, Amazon had already paid out more than $845 million in redress to consumers. The revised order makes consumers who used between 11 and 20 Prime benefits during a one‑year period eligible for automatic refunds, a group that was not included in earlier payment phases. Those refunds will be delivered electronically via Venmo or PayPal or by mailed check, with no claim forms or additional paperwork required. If the aggregate amount paid does not reach a specified threshold by February 2027, Amazon will issue an extra $149 to consumers who have already received a refund, bringing the maximum possible payment to $200. Those supplemental payments are scheduled to begin by April 2027 and will also be distributed automatically.
“The revised order will ensure more consumers who were harmed by Amazon’s deceptive enrollment and cancellation practices benefit from the FTC’s historic settlement,” Christopher Mufarrige, Director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection said.
“This action underscores the FTC’s commitment to ensuring companies return money to consumers harmed by unlawful and deceptive business practices,” Christopher Mufarrige, Director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection said.
The FTC’s September 2025 settlement required Amazon to provide up to $1.5 billion in redress for deceptive Prime enrollment and a separate $1 billion civil penalty. By September 2026 the company had distributed more than $845 million of that redress, prompting the joint motion to accelerate and expand payments.
Source: FTC Press Releases (https://ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2026/09/ftc-announces-additional-payments-consumers-stemming-ftcs-amazon-prime-settlement)

item.title: FleetCor agrees to pay $100 million to settle FTC action over hidden fuel‑card fees
item.description:
FleetCor and its CEO have agreed to pay $100 million to resolve an FTC administrative action over undisclosed fees on fuel cards used by small businesses. The settlement follows a 2023 federal district court summary judgment that found FleetCor charged hidden fees and misrepresented fuel‑card savings, a ruling upheld by an appeals court in 2026.
The $100 million will be used to provide redress to FleetCor’s business customers who were harmed by the undisclosed fees. FleetCor and Clarke also agreed not to oppose reimposition of a federal court injunction against Clarke. Under the consent order, FleetCor may not bill a customer for any charge without obtaining the customer’s express informed consent and providing clear, unavoidable information about that charge. The order further bars the company from hiding charge details behind hyperlinks and from making deceptive claims about the gas savings or fraud‑control features of its fuel cards.
“FleetCor deceived its small business customers by promising fuel savings that never materialized, while unfairly charging them hidden and unauthorized fees,” said Christopher Mufarrige, Director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection,” Christopher Mufarrige, Director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection said.
The FTC first filed a complaint against FleetCor in federal court in 2019, alleging that the company imposed unauthorized fees and misrepresented the benefits of its fuel cards. In 2023, a federal district court granted summary judgment to the FTC on all counts, finding that FleetCor had charged hidden fees and misrepresented gas savings. A federal appeals court affirmed that judgment in 2026, upholding the permanent injunction against the company.
Source: FTC Press Releases (https://ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2026/09/fleetcor-agrees-pay-100-million-resolve-administrative-action-after-federal-court-finds-it-violated)

item.title: Next raises profit forecast for fourth time this year as H1 beats expectations
item.description:
Next has raised its full‑year profit guidance for the fourth time in 2026, lifting the forecast by £12 million to £1.255 billion after stronger‑than‑expected first‑half results. In the first half of financial year 2026, group sales rose 9 % to £3.54 billion and pre‑tax profit climbed 10.5 % to £569 million.
Online sales grew 7.4 % while store sales slipped 1.7 %, reflecting the shift toward digital channels; international sales jumped 24 % despite Middle‑East disruptions, driven by effective digital marketing that yielded £1.77 profit per pound spent. The company cited warehouse‑capacity investments and cost savings as contributors to the uplift. Looking ahead, Next expects its new AI tools, an AI Business Analysts agent and a Coding agent, to boost development productivity by at least 30 % over the next two years, and it believes AI could cut the cost of modernising its legacy mainframe from £50 million to £10 million. Next also trimmed its second‑half UK sales growth outlook from 2.8 % to 2 %, warning that higher taxes in the upcoming Autumn Budget could stifle growth and urging the government to control spending or stimulate the economy.
“The result of a small upgrade in sales expectations and some additional cost savings, mainly in warehousing,” Next said.
“The tax burden is at its highest level for over 60 years, and seems to us to be at the point where further increases only risk stifling growth – and lower growth is likely to only worsen Government finances – a vicious circle,” Next said.
Next has raised its profit guidance for the full year – for the fourth time this year. The company warned in February that it was expecting disruption in the Middle East to impact on its sales, with prices in that region rising because of it.
Source: InternetRetailing (https://internetretailing.net/next-raises-profit-forecast-for-fourth-time-this-year-as-h1-beats-expectations)

item.title: FreightWaves analysts warn US trucking market stays fragile as STRI jumps 75 basis points
item.description:
At a New York shipper gathering on Tuesday, FreightWaves analysts Craig Fuller and Zach Strickland said the US trucking market remains fragile, noting the Sonar Tender Rejection Index fell below 14% after exceeding 17% in June. Strickland pointed out that the index has risen roughly 75 basis points in the last week, signaling renewed volatility.
He added that tender rejection rates have been climbing since November 2025, even as shippers shift more freight to intermodal rail services. Fuller noted that J.B. Hunt’s CEO Shelley Simpson also sees the market as fragile, but views tight capacity as a source of potential upside rather than pure risk. He added that while his Wall Street contacts warn of a disorderly supply chain reminiscent of COVID, the current freight environment remains orderly according to container‑ship data.
“The end result, he added, is “a new baseline.” But even that might not stick, Strickland said, citing the sharp move up in the STRI, which has gone up about 75 basis points in just the past week,” Zach Strickland, director of market intelligence, FreightWaves/SONAR said.
“Fuller said his Wall Street contacts are expressing concern about a “disorderly” supply chain reminiscent of COVID days. But he said that is not going to happen,” Craig Fuller, CEO, FreightWaves said.
Earlier State of Freight webinars in early 2026 had depicted a market advancing in large increments, but the analysts said they were now measuring a market that was not moving higher. The New York shipper meeting was sponsored by Cass Information Systems and SONAR. They attributed the description of the market as fragile to the recent movement in the Sonar Tender Rejection Index.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/at-shippers-confab-defining-a-fragile-trucking-market)

item.title: The Entertainer partners with THG Commerce to launch AI-powered platform in spring 2027
item.description:
The Entertainer has appointed THG Commerce to build a new digital platform featuring AI-powered shopping assistance, set to launch in spring 2027. The multi‑year partnership will draw on THG Ingenuity’s work with Google Cloud, using Vertex AI Commerce Search and Gemini to power conversational discovery and intent‑based search.
The overhaul includes a refreshed web and mobile storefront alongside an upgraded Click & Collect service intended to link online browsing with in‑store pickup. Personalised recommendations, richer editorial content and curated product journeys will be added to help parents, gift buyers and adult collectors navigate the retailer’s extensive toy range. Further phases will expand the platform into loyalty programmes, retail media and social commerce, building on the initial AI search and discovery tools. The Entertainer aims to combine its toy expertise and brand portfolio with AI tools that simplify product discovery for shoppers.
“Our ambition is to redefine the experience for anyone looking to discover and buy toys, whether they are shopping for their children, choosing a gift for someone else or buying for themselves. Toy shopping should be joyful and inspiring, but the sheet breadth of choice means customers increasingly need help navigating it,” Malcolm Carter, Digital & Marketing Director, The Entertainer said.
“The Entertainer get AI-enabled shopping assistance and CRM-integrated enhanced personalisation at launch, then a roadmap into loyalty, retail media and social commerce, backed by our wider THG Studios capabilities, which can bring a new range to life on site quickly,” Darren Rajanah, Chief Revenue Officer, THG Ingenuity said.
Earlier this year, fast-fashion retailer Shein teamed up with THG Fulfil, another arm of THG Ingenuity, to introduce fulfilment and logistics support for sellers on its UK marketplace.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/09/the-entertainer-plots-major-ecommerce-overhaul-with-ai-powered-shopping-tools)

item.title: WSG Brands buys Nasty Gal for $16 million
item.description:
WSG Brands announced Tuesday it has acquired Nasty Gal from Debenhams Group for $16 million. Nasty Gal generated £12 million in gross merchandise value last year, about $16 million at press time. The brand also reported £400,000 in adjusted EBITDA over the same period.
Debenhams said the brand’s results were not material to the company and the sale aligns with its strategy to shift to a marketplace‑led model that uses less capital. WSG Brands plans to expand Nasty Gal’s assortment to include denim, footwear and bags, jewelry, activewear, swimwear, sleepwear, beauty, travel and additional lifestyle categories, mainly through licensing deals. The company earlier this year bought Allbirds in partnership with Aerosoles owner American Exchange Group, and acquired streetwear label Von Dutch two years ago.
“We see a tremendous opportunity to build upon that foundation, introduce the brand to a new generation of consumers and expand Nasty Gal into a global lifestyle brand while staying true to the attitude and individuality that have always defined it,” Jack Cheika, founder and CEO of WSG Brands said.
Boohoo was the sole bidder at the auction conducted as part of Nasty Gal’s 2016 bankruptcy. WSG Brands said in a press release Tuesday.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/allbirds-ip-owner-wsg-brands-buys-nasty-gal-sixteen-million/830520)

item.title: Lowe’s promotes CMO Jen Wilson to executive VP, adds digital commerce as online sales jump 15.7%
item.description:
Lowe’s earlier this month promoted Chief Marketing Officer Jen Wilson to executive vice president, adding digital commerce to her remit as online sales rose 15.7% More than 80% of home improvement shopping begins online, highlighting the need for a unified digital experience
In her expanded role, Wilson now oversees Lowe’s website and its third‑party Marketplace, in addition to marketing, retail media, loyalty, and personalization. She will join the company’s executive leadership team, reporting directly to the CEO as part of the senior‑level strategy group. The promotion follows a period in which Lowe’s comparable sales grew just 0.2% in Q2 2026 while online sales surged 15.7%, underscoring the channel’s growing importance.
“It was really important for Lowe’s, and it’s important for our customer, to be able to deliver that consistent experience,” Jen Wilson, Chief Marketing Officer said.
“More than 80% of all home improvement shopping starts online,” Jen Wilson, Chief Marketing Officer said.
Wilson has been with Lowe’s for more than two decades and was named chief marketer in June 2024 after leading the paint business and other merchandising roles. Before this promotion she had overseen the development of a loyalty program, a retail media network, and a creator network launched the prior year.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/lowes-chief-marketing-officer-jen-wilson-leads-digital-commerce/830444)

item.title: Carter’s launches 60‑second “Watch Them Glow” spot to refresh brand for Gen Z parents
item.description:
Carter’s launched its “Watch Them Glow” campaign on Tuesday with a 60‑second television and digital spot aimed at connecting with Gen Z and millennial parents. The spot introduces a new logo that replaces the apostrophe with a shooting star and is part of a broader identity refresh rolling out this year, with further updates to retail, product and packaging slated for 2027.
The campaign also includes a revamped social media strategy, a creator program called Light Makers, and multiyear partnerships with organizations that support children and families. It will air on connected TV platforms such as Nexxen, Roku, Disney+ and Hulu, as well as on Carter’s own digital and social channels. Carter’s says the refresh is grounded in Pew Research Center findings that nearly half of U.S. parents are raising their children differently than they were raised, emphasizing acceptance and individual paths. The move follows the company’s decision to increase marketing spend this year, a step executives linked to recent revenue gains.
“This is a job to be done over multiple years,” she said,” Chief Marketing Officer Sarah Crockett said.
“Today’s generation of parents are really embracing this notion of self-expression,” Crockett said,” Chief Marketing Officer Sarah Crockett said.
Carter’s had not updated its logo since 2000, making this the brand’s first new logo in over two decades. The work follows plans by parent Carter’s, Inc. to increase marketing spend this year, a move that executives said has already contributed to recent revenue gains.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/carters-refreshing-brand-gen-z-millennial-parents/830443)

item.title: Senate poised to vote on retail crime bill that would expand ICE role
item.description:
The Senate is expected to vote on the Combating Organized Retail Crime Act by the end of the year after the House passed it in May. The legislation would establish a Supply Chain Crime Coordination Center inside Homeland Security Investigations, whose head would be appointed by ICE’s director.
Many retailers and loss prevention experts back the bill because it would improve coordination among local, state, federal law enforcement and the private sector to combat organized retail crime. However, critics warn that the measure could pull retailers into immigration enforcement efforts unrelated to theft, as HSI resources are already being diverted to support mass deportations. The National Retail Federation told Retail Dive it avoided questions about ICE’s role and the shift of HSI resources to immigration enforcement. The NRF also disclosed that it halted its annual impact assessment in 2023 after Retail Dive found it had combined outdated shrink estimates unrelated to crime.
“I see people talk about organized retail theft, but we have really not a lot of strong understanding of what's driving it and the scope of the problem, and whether or not the actual problem is getting bigger,” Jeff Asher, crime analyst and co-founder of AH Datalytics said.
“Through this, retailers are going to be deputized to help ICE,” Jina John, Senior Policy Counsel for AI, Privacy, and Technology at the American Civil Liberties Union said.
CORCA has been a top goal of retail industry lobbyists for years and enjoys bipartisan support in both the House and Senate. The House passed the bill in May, leading to an expected Senate vote before the year’s end. Proponents argue the legislation would improve coordination against organized retail theft.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/how-the-retail-crime-bill-could-bolster-ice/829731)

item.title: Amazon grants U.S. employees 10% online and 20% in-store grocery discount starting Oct. 1, 2026
item.description:
Starting October 1, 2026, Amazon will give every U.S. employee a 10% discount on groceries bought through Amazon.com and Whole Foods Market Online and a 20% discount on in-store purchases at Whole Foods Market and Daily Shop. The discount has no spending cap, requires no minimum purchase, and is available from an employee's first day on the job.
It applies to fresh produce, dairy, diapers, baby formula, cleaning supplies, pet food and other everyday essentials sold and shipped by Amazon or offered through Whole Foods Market. Employees can combine the discount with Prime member prices, coupons, Lightning Deals, Subscribe & Save and other promotions. Whole Foods Market operates more than 550 stores nationwide, with over 100 additional locations in development, including the Daily Shop format for quick trips. Since adding perishables to Same-Day Delivery in early 2025, sales of those items have grown more than forty‑fold and now represent nine of the top ten most‑ordered Same‑Day Delivery products where the service is offered.
Amazon has long sought to make grocery shopping faster and more affordable, offering Same-Day Delivery in more than 2,300 U.S. cities and towns and expanding its Whole Foods Market footprint. The company already sells nearly three million grocery and everyday essential items on Amazon.com and continues to develop new store concepts like Daily Shop for quick trips.
Source: About Amazon (https://aboutamazon.com/news/workplace/amazon-us-employee-grocery-discount)

item.title: Amazon raises U.S. full-time core operations starting pay to $20/hour
item.description:
Amazon announced that the minimum starting pay for U.S. full-time core operations employees will increase to $20 per hour, with average pay reaching nearly $24 per hour. When the value of benefits is factored in, average total compensation tops $32 per hour.
Employees will also receive an uncapped 10% discount on fresh groceries and everyday essentials bought online through Amazon.com and Whole Foods Market Online, plus a 20% discount for in‑store purchases at Whole Foods Market. A new lifetime banking benefit, Day 1 Financial, provides qualified workers and their families with fee‑free checking and savings accounts through First Tech Federal Credit Union, including surcharge‑free ATM access and credit‑building programs. Amazon continues to offer existing perks such as a free Prime membership, healthcare plans as low as $5 a week with $5 copays, and prepaid education assistance. Pay will rise automatically each year for the first three years of employment under an annual step plan.
I often hear that they appreciate a good paycheck, but also really value the full range of benefits that we offer—which together help them support their families and grow in the long run. So, each year, we look at that full picture—pay, benefits, and how we can continue to support them and their families through many different parts of their lives.
