item.title: Census Bureau Announces September 28, 2026 Revision Date for Retail Sales Estimates
item.description:
The U.S. Census Bureau said it will release revised not-adjusted and adjusted monthly retail sales estimates on September 28, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. EDT. It also said the July 2026 Monthly State Retail Sales report will be published on November 16, 2026.
The Advance Monthly and Monthly Retail Trade Surveys, the Annual Retail Trade Survey, and the Quarterly E-Commerce Report together constitute the Census Bureau's most comprehensive source of U.S. retail economic activity data. The Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis noted that its FRED mobile application now incorporates the Census Bureau's 13 key economic indicators. The Census Bureau updated its API for economic indicators by adding a /timeseries/ endpoint to facilitate time-series access. Users can find examples of the new API calls on the Bureau's Developers' webpage.
Earlier announcements indicated that monthly retail estimates are anticipated to be revised based on historical corrections and the results of the 2023 and 2024 Annual Integrated Economic Survey. The Bureau added that the July 2026 MSRS release will include an annual update incorporating revisions of the Monthly Retail Trade Survey sales estimates and other methodological improvements. It also pointed users to the Economic Indicator Release Schedule for all 2025/2026 release dates and promoted the FRED App for Apple and Android devices.
Source: U.S. Census Bureau — Retail / Ecommerce (https://census.gov/retail/index.html)

item.title: Shipium launches Always On Audit for real-time freight invoice monitoring
item.description:
Shipium has launched Always On Audit, an AI-driven system that provides continuous, real-time monitoring of every shipment. It replaces the traditional month-old invoice reconciliation process with ongoing checks that flag discrepancies as shipments move.
The system creates a digital twin of each shipment at the moment it is rated and routed, capturing expected cost, dimensions and carrier contract terms. As the shipment progresses, data from rating, carrier selection, label printing and delivery are written to that twin in real time. When the AI detects a mismatch, it surfaces the exception for human review, and the outcome is fed back to improve the model.
“Monthly audit and continuous audit are not the same job at different speeds,” Penny Allen, SVP of AI Product and Engineering, Shipium said.
“We think of ourselves as the rails for shipping,” Jason Murray, CEO and co-founder, Shipium said.
Freight audit has long been one of the least glamorous corners of supply chain operations. It traditionally involves boxes of paper or a team hunched over spreadsheets reconciling invoices weeks after the shipments in question have already been delivered.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/shipium-rethinks-freight-audit-as-forensics-not-archaeology)

item.title: Bonobos launches fall campaign with Jack Quaid series
item.description:
Bonobos launched its fall campaign on Thursday, centering it on “The Weekday Warrior Show,” an episodic content series starring Jack Quaid. The series will run across Bonobos’ digital and social channels through the season and is built to move audiences toward the brand’s website. The campaign uses sitcom-style humor, real Bonobos employees, and product-focused episodes to connect social content with Bonobos’ fall collection.
In the first episode, Quaid dubs himself the “weekday warrior consultant” while promoting the Weekday Warrior Pant, which Bonobos describes as having the polish of a dress pant but the comfort of a chino. The series is designed to be social-first, with episodic content and bite-sized versions for paid media, then points viewers toward Bonobos’ website for video and other supplemental material. Future installments will feature other fall products, including dress shirts, oxford shirts, and blazers.
“Jack brings such a unique personality and is able to represent that person who can be calm in the midst of the storm of the workday chaos, but doing it in a way that is completely effortless, which ties to the product,,” Joe Berean, Bonobos Chief Marketing Officer said.
“[The series] is architected to be digital first, with a high focus on social, but in a way that can be appreciated and enjoyed episodically or through the more bite-sized content pieces that we know perform so well through a lot of our paid media channels,,” Joe Berean, Bonobos Chief Marketing Officer said.
Bonobos launched in 2007 and pioneered a direct-to-consumer model, but the brand was later bought and sold by Walmart. Bonobos and Express were bought out of bankruptcy in 2024 by Phoenix Retail, a joint venture from Simon Property Group, Brookfield Properties, Centennial, and WHP Global.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/why-bonobos-fall-campaign-centers-on-episodic-content-with-jack-quaid/830071)

item.title: Lawmakers reintroduce FABRIC Act with $100 million for U.S. garment grants
item.description:
On Monday, Rep. Jerrold Nadler and Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand reintroduced the FABRIC Act, proposing $100 million in domestic manufacturing grants to support over 75,000 U.S. garment workers. The grant amount doubles the $50 million sought in the prior version and would create a brand guarantor liability for Fair Labor Standards Act violations across subcontracting tiers.
Under the bill, garment workers covered by the Fair Labor Standards Act could no longer receive piece-rate or per-unit base pay, though productivity bonuses tied to output could still be paid on top of an hourly wage. A limited exception would apply to workers under collective‑bargaining agreements that meet specified wage, overtime and dispute‑resolution standards. The statutory floor would remain the federal minimum wage of $7.25 an hour, unchanged since 2009, with employers still required to follow higher state or local minimums where they apply. The legislation does not revive the 30 percent tax credit for moving operations to HUBZones or low‑income communities that appeared in the original 2022 House version.
“America’s garment workers have been undervalued and subjected to unfair labor practices for far too long, due to weak regulations across the fashion industry and the rise of fast fashion,” Rep. Jerrold Nadler said.
“With more than 100,000 New Yorkers contributing their labor to a billion-dollar garment industry, it is time to protect these workers and others across our nation and make historic investments in domestic manufacturing by passing the FABRIC Act,” Rep. Jerrold Nadler said.
The bill has been introduced before, first appearing in the 117th Congress in 2022. It was revived in September 2023 but stalled in committee both times. This marks the third attempt to pass the FABRIC Act through Congress.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/fabric-act-garment-workers-piece-rate-brand-liability-grant-1239234683)

item.title: MiKargo247 and Verified Carrier launch spot cargo insurance for strategic cargo theft
item.description:
On Sept. 1, MiKargo247 and Verified Carrier announced a partnership that lets brokers buy MiKargo247 spot cargo insurance and have the strategic theft exclusion removed when the load is hauled by an eligible verified carrier. Strategic cargo theft made up about 30% of reported U.S. cargo theft incidents in 2025, according to a June report from Munich Re Specialty and BSI Consulting.
MiKargo247’s spot cargo policy, which it has offered since entering the market in 2022, provides on‑demand, single‑trip coverage with limits of up to $1 million per load. Brokers can initiate the process inside the Verified Carrier platform, where they verify a carrier, quote and bind the MiKargo247 policy, and download a certificate without leaving the workflow. Verified Carrier’s service focuses on confirming that the carrier involved in a freight transaction is legitimate before pickup, using driver and carrier verification tools. The partnership combines verification with insurance so that verified carriers are not penalized by exclusions meant for fraudulent actors.
“The strategic theft exclusion has always been a risk management decision, not a permanent limitation,” Michele McGinnis, CEO of MiKargo247, said in the announcement,” Michele McGinnis, CEO of MiKargo247 said.
“Verified Carrier exists because the freight industry needs a way to protect carriers, brokers, shippers, and their customers by making fraud structurally impossible at every link in the chain,” Panfilov said in the announcement,” Alex Panfilov, founder and CEO of Verified Carrier said.
Before this partnership, MiKargo247 offered spot cargo insurance that excluded strategic theft, and Verified Carrier provided carrier verification services but did not include insurance coverage.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/mikargo247-verified-carrier-launch-coverage-for-strategic-cargo-theft)

item.title: Target to open eight stores on Oct. 11, completing its 30‑store 2024 plan
item.description:
Target is set to open eight new stores on October 11 in New York, Ohio, Mississippi, Texas, Virginia, and Tennessee. Seven of the eight stores will exceed 125,000 square feet, surpassing the chain’s average store size.
These openings mark the final batch of the 30 locations Target planned to add in 2024.
“These new stores give our teams the tools and environments to bring our merchandising strengths to life, create easier and more inspiring shopping experiences, and use technology to move smarter and faster every day,” Adrienne Costanzo, chief stores officer at Target said.
Earlier this year Target opened its 2,000th store in Fuquay‑Varina, North Carolina, and had announced six more store openings for May in Arizona, Missouri, New Jersey, and North Carolina.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/target-opens-eight-stores-fall/830411)

item.title: Old Navy launches Sport subbrand with shop‑in‑shops in over 40 stores
item.description:
Old Navy has consolidated its activewear assortment into a new subbrand called Old Navy Sport, Gap Inc. announced Tuesday. The line will be available in every Old Navy location, featuring dedicated shop‑in‑shops in more than 40 stores and a dedicated rollout of 42 immersive shop‑in‑shops.
The subbrand offers refreshed seasonal styles, updated colors and modern silhouettes aimed at delivering performance and value. Old Navy, which has faced sales challenges this year under a new CEO, is currently ranked fifth in the U.S. activewear market according to Circana data. Health‑focused consumers are growing, with 70% saying health is more important than a year ago, and Old Navy’s price‑point strategy has kept it among the top five activewear sellers. The rollout includes online, the app, stores nationwide, and a new @OldNavySport social handle.
“The customer is much more active than it ever has been,” Jessica Ramírez, co‑founder and managing director of The Consumer Collective said.
“Our denim category, active category, kids and baby — these are the areas of strength for our brand and the areas that you're going to see more and more marketing as the weeks go by, and ultimately become the important categories that drive the back half,” Richard Dickson, CEO of Gap Inc said.
Old Navy’s activewear has been a key strength amid weaker summer dress sales, according to Gap Inc. CEO Richard Dickson at the Goldman Sachs conference. Meanwhile, Gap Inc.’s Athleta and Lululemon brands have faced declines, prompting both to hire Nike veterans to lead turnarounds. Analysts note that while some see the activewear category waning, competition has intensified as more players enter the space.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/old-navy-sport-activewear-new-subbrand/830384)

item.title: El Caficultor turns coffee packaging into direct subscription channel via AuraVeo QR codes
item.description:
El Caficultor launched a QR‑code‑driven subscription channel for its four‑origin 100% Arábica coffee range at London Packaging Week on 16‑17 September. The initial rollout covers the brand’s four 100% Arábica origins: Cerrado Dulce (Brazil), Sidamo (Ethiopia), La Vereda (Colombia) and Selva Negra (Nicaragua). Scanning the unique QR code on each pack reveals farm, altitude, processing method and flavour details before presenting a discounted subscription offer.
The cloud‑based AuraVeo platform lets El Caficultor update the QR‑code content without reprinting packages and track interactions at the SKU level. Consumers who scan the code can opt in to share first‑party data, giving the brand insights into engagement and purchasing behaviour. Appetite Creative placed the QR code inside a country‑map illustration on the front of the pack and added the call‑to‑action “ESCANEA Y AHORRA” (“Scan and Save”) to drive scans.
“Brands put a great deal of valuable information into their products, but much of it disappears once those products reach the shelf. El Caficultor’s packaging is no longer just a container; it’s now a sales channel. “The important point is that the QR code is not simply a link. It gives the brand a way to keep the experience current, understand consumer behaviour, and give an interested customer a clear next step,” Sandra Wagner, CEO of AuraVeo said.
“Someone buys our coffee, enjoys it, and then we lose them; that has always been the frustration of selling through retail. Now the moment they scan the bag they can read the story of that specific origin and subscribe at a better price, in the same thirty seconds,” Julián A. Lozano Sánchez, general manager at Indian EcoTrade and El Caficultor said.
Source: InternetRetailing (https://internetretailing.net/auraveo-turns-el-caficultor-coffee-packaging-into-direct-subscription-channel)

item.title: Amazon and Target launch competing October sales events on Oct. 6‑7
item.description:
Amazon and Target announced that their competing October sale events will run from Oct. 6 to Oct. 7, according to company press releases issued Tuesday. Amazon’s Big Deal Days will be available to paid Prime members and will feature new product drops each day across categories such as fragrances, Shark appliances and select groceries, while Target’s Circle Deal Days will be open to free loyalty members, with Target Circle 360 subscribers gaining early access a day prior. Target reported Q2 net sales of $26.5 billion, up 5.3% year over year, and Amazon’s Q2 online store sales reached $70.4 billion, a 15% increase, with physical store sales up 4% to $5.8 billion.
Amazon’s event will also highlight a new FAO Schwarz storefront and holiday gift lists designed to help shoppers prepare for hosting, decorating and gifting.;Target’s Circle Deal Days will emphasize deals on its private‑label brands, including kids’ clothing line Cat & Jack and furniture line Threshold.;Both retailers are positioning the October sales as a way to capture early holiday spending before the traditional November‑December peak.
“Once fall arrives, there's so much to get ready for — the hosting, the decorating, the holiday gifting — and Prime Big Deal Days makes it easy to check it all off while saving,” Carmen Nestares, Amazon’s vice president of North America marketing and Prime tech said.
Amazon held its annual Prime Day sales event in June, marking a slightly earlier run from its usual July dates.;The leaves are just starting to fall in parts of the U.S., meaning it's that time of year again when major retailers — like Target and Walmart — often compete with e-commerce giant Amazon during sales events.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/dueling-amazon-target-october-sales-events-return/830402)

item.title: Burlington expands on-site solar across distribution network, adding two California sites slated for 2026
item.description:
Burlington expanded several on-site solar installations across its distribution center network, according to its 2025 Corporate Social Responsibility report published this year. By the end of fiscal year 2025, which concluded Jan. 31, 2026, the retailer advanced plans for solar at a new Georgia distribution center and an upcoming Arizona facility, and it aims to add solar at two new California centers slated for 2026.
Burlington reported that 25% of its electricity consumption came from renewable resources in fiscal year 2025, exceeding its 2030 goal of 20%. By the end of that fiscal year, the retailer had executed on-site solar agreements in New Jersey, California and Massachusetts. It also broadened renewable electricity supply agreements across the Midwest, Mid-Atlantic and West Coast during the period. The company did not disclose further specifics on the Ellabell, Georgia and Arizona projects and declined to comment when approached.
Burlington has been making efforts to increase the use of renewable energy across its operations. As part of its sustainability push, the retailer has been making significant investments in solar power beyond distribution sites.
Source: Supply Chain Dive (https://supplychaindive.com/news/burlington-advances-on-site-solar-strategy-across-distribution-network/829942)

item.title: Designer Brands tests The Edit shop-in-shop at four DSW locations
item.description:
Designer Brands is piloting The Edit, a store-within-a-store concept, in four DSW locations this fall, according to CEO Doug Howe. Each Edit shop will occupy between 1,000 and 1,500 square feet inside the existing DSW stores.
The Edit will showcase a curated selection of affordable luxury and elevated fashion brands in an open, experiential environment. Designer Brands will use the pilot to assess customer response and shape any future expansion of the concept. In the second quarter of 2026, the company reported consolidated net sales of $730.6 million, a 1.2% year‑over‑year decline, with retail sales down 2.2% and comparable store sales down 2.6%. Designer Brands also said it lowered its debt to $423.1 million for Q2 2026, $93 million less than a year earlier, and is relaunching its loyalty program this month, noting that nearly 90% of transactions come from its roughly 30 million VIP members. The company also noted that its Topo Athletic brand is on track to generate more than $100 million in sales by 2027, with growth expected in both existing and new distribution channels.
“Nearly 90% of our transactions come from our approximately 30 million VIP members, and we have significantly modernized the program, enhancing the value we provide to our VIPs while improving the effectiveness and efficiency of our CRM efforts,” Howe said,” Doug Howe, CEO of Designer Brands said.
As of August 1, Designer Brands operated 668 stores across three banners and reported that its brand portfolio, including Topo Athletic, Keds, Vince Camuto and Jessica Simpson, had grown nearly 18% year over year in the second quarter. The company raised its full‑year 2026 sales guidance to a range of flat to up 1% year over year, up from the prior outlook of down 1% to up 1%. In February, Designer Brands announced an unspecified number of layoffs aimed at strengthening its ability to execute, manage costs, and create long‑term value.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/dsw-tests-the-edit-store-concept-shop-in-shop/830406)

item.title: Target names ex-Hilton CMO Mark Weinstein as chief marketing and guest experience officer
item.description:
Target on Monday named Mark Weinstein as its chief marketing and guest experience officer, effective immediately. In the role, Weinstein will oversee Target’s retail media network Roundel and its Target+ marketplace while also leading the company’s marketing, loyalty and guest experience strategies.
He will report to Target’s chief executive officer, Michael Fiddelke. Prior to joining Target, Weinstein accumulated over 16 years at Hilton, most recently serving as its global chief marketing officer starting in 2020. Target posted a 3.8% gain in comparable sales and a 3.6% increase in traffic during the second quarter. The chief marketing officer role has been empty since Lisa Roath transitioned from that post to lead the food, essentials and beauty division early last year. In his new role, Weinstein will focus on shaping how consumers experience and engage with Target across its channels, culture and community. During his time at Hilton, he managed the Hilton Honors loyalty program and oversaw the retailer’s 28 brands, including its luxury lines.
“Mark has a proven ability to understand what consumers value and turn those insights into brand connections that feel relevant and personal,” Fiddelke said in a statement,” Michael Fiddelke, Target CEO said.
Before the appointment, Target had recorded a 3.8% rise in comparable sales and a 3.6% increase in traffic for the second quarter. The retailer had been without a chief marketing officer since Lisa Roath was moved from that role to oversee food, essentials and beauty early last year.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/target-hires-ex-hilton-cmo-as-chief-marketing-and-guest-experience-officer/830355)

item.title: Old Navy partners with MrBeast, driving over 22% traffic jump to kids’ assortment
item.description:
Old Navy partnered with MrBeast for its 2026 back-to-school campaign, which drove an over 22% jump in traffic to the kids’ assortment online in the days immediately following launch. The MrBeast videos generated over 100 million global views and 1.4 billion impressions on YouTube.
The campaign features comedic content, sweepstakes and giveaways that include free lunch for a year to a middle school in Kansas and cash prizes plus Old Navy gift cards for students who answer meme-themed trivia correctly. It marks Old Navy’s first back-to-school effort anchored on a single creator, part of a broader shift away from highly produced ads toward authentic storytelling aimed at Gen Z and Gen Alpha shoppers. Old Navy has also been rewiring its marketing after a 4% decline in comparable sales in Q2, with Gap Inc. CEO Richard Dickson citing the MrBeast collaboration and a recent Cardi B denim campaign as signs of a more effective approach.
“The numbers are staggering,” Berger said,” Damon Berger, senior vice president and head of shared marketing services at Gap Inc said.
“With improved execution in August, we have seen the business pick up, reinforcing our confidence in the actions we are taking,” Dickson said on the Q2 earnings call,” Richard Dickson, CEO of Gap Inc said.
The previous back-to-school campaigns are those more highly produced ideas. Now this is about more storytelling from the authentic lens to the communities that we're trying to reach, Berger said. Old Navy recently named Michael Francis as CEO, replacing Haio Barbeito as part of a planned transition. Among surveyed parents, 91% report their teenage children influence their brand preferences, research from HarrisX and Allison Worldwide found.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/old-navys-mrbeast-marketing-deal-boosts-engagement/830255)
